_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/2/3 (Series A2DDC/2, booklet code 2131/2/3), sibling of the opener 31/2/1. plan.txt gave no skip list (no numbered scheme cells), so shared questions were matched by CONTENT against data/2024-31-2-1.questions.json and each was confirmed on this paper's own page before its text was reused. 24 page images (cover announces 23 printed pages; idx 23, folio 24, is BLANK, confirmed at full size). idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-22, Hindi on every odd index 1-21; odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet, all Hindi, and every English page ends on a whole question, so the parity holds throughout. Instructions confirm sci80: 39 questions, A Q1-20 MCQ x1, B Q21-26 x2, C Q27-33 x3, D Q34-36 x5, E Q37-39 case-based x4. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (single-set file, every page footed 'X SCIENCE 31/2/3', ms pages 2-10) for a bare OR: after Q21, 25, 30, 31, 34, 36, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. Q29 and Q35 print (a) and (b) with NO OR and one marks figure, and the scheme awards both parts toward one total, so each is one row. Section E prints its alternatives as '(c) ... OR (c) ...', so questionNumber is '37 (c)' / '37 (c) OR' and refs follow the corpus style Q37ci/Q37cii. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme as images; each was re-derived and all 20 agree. No void or award-regardless note anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points on this paper are ORDINARY full stops (2.25, 0.5, 0.25, 0.1). Q11 (= 31/2/1 Q8) prints 'true' WITHOUT the underline 31/2/1 carries; that is emphasis only, so the 31/2/1 text was reused byte for byte so the row dedups.

questions.context: When electric current flows in a purely resistive circuit electrical energy gets fully converted into heat energy. The amount of heat produced (H) in the circuit is found to be directly proportional to (i) the square of current \((I^2)\) (ii) the resistance (R) of the conductor and (iii) the time (t) for which current flows. In other words \(H = I^2Rt\). Electrical devices such an electric fuse, electric heater, electric iron etc. are all based on this effect called heating effect of electric current.
